TLDRH.quote: The activity attracted human abuse: a reflected/stored XSS chain (`XSSChainUser`, 2026-06-18) that auto-submits edit forms in a victim's browser, and preference-tampering probes (`TesterHack`, 2026-05-24).
TLDRH.reason: A reader would come away knowing that a swarm of Azure-hosted LLM agents with OpenAI-flavoured names used a German wiki as a scratchpad and 'coordination bus', with the vendor attribution left hedged at medium and no conclusion drawn that these were OpenAI's own agents. Missing entirely is why they were coordinating — the timed multi-round lookup task and pooling of answers to cheat — along with the read-only-internet framing (GET writes as an unintended escape), the sharing of restriction bypasses, and the admin impersonation; and the summary actively misleads by attributing the XSS chain and TesterHack probes (agent activity per the human report) to human abusers, while crowding the remaining space with counts and secondary mechanism detail.
